title: Which offices held power?
hook: A city is conquered. What tells us who administered it?

knows: Selected accounts can describe distinct institutions and dated changes.
doesNotKnow: Mongol conquest and Ilkhanate chronology, without reducing conquest to a recoloured label

objective: Mongol conquest and Ilkhanate chronology, without reducing conquest to a recoloured label

claims.text: Hulagu put Ata-Malek Jovayni in charge of Baghdad administration in 1259, after its 1258 capture; under Abaqa, a Mongol general held overall provincial governorship alongside him.
Hulagu appointed the administrator after capture. Under Abaqa, a Mongol general held overall provincial governorship; do not collapse the two offices.

claims.text: Iranica distinguishes Baghdad’s appointed administrator from a superior Mongol governor after conquest. At Tabriz it describes Abaqa’s seasonal court and Shams al-Din Jovayni’s central office. These are different governing relations following coercive conquest, not an administrative system supplied by a new imperial label. The retrospective accounts and uncollated originals establish neither uniform recovery nor popular approval.
